To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lead nitrate added to soil in solution does not equilibrate with soil and worms accumulate lead over the duration of the test period.

(i) the bioavailability of lead in artificially Pb-amended soil decreases as the equilibration period of the soil with the added Pb increases; (ii) the bioaccumulation of Pb in worms is time dependent; and (iii) the toxicity of lead to worms is time dependent.
The bioavailability of Pb in soil is reduced with time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of time on the toxicity and bioavailability of Pb in artificially contaminated soils.
the influence of time on the toxicity of lead to earthworms.
the development of an environmentally relevant test to assess the toxicity of contaminants in soils to worms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OECD acute worm toxicity protocol is inadequate for assessing the toxicity of Pb.
the OECD acute toxicity test does not accurately reflect the environmental relevance of lead toxicity and bio-accumulation in soil.
the current OECD acute worm test is inadequate for the purpose of determining the toxicity of contaminants to soil invertebrates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OECD test is not fit for the purpose it is intended.
the OECD acute earthworm toxicity test does not adequately reflect the toxicity of Pb in soil.
the OECD earthworm test should be amended so that the equilibration period of the test soil is at least 35 days and that the test should be terminated after 14 days.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to take the time factor into consideration when conducting toxicity studies with earthworms in artificially contaminated soil.
the time to death in the standard acute toxicity tests is not a reliable measure of the time taken for the test organism to accumulate a toxic dose of the chemical in its body.
lead toxicity to earthworms is time-dependent.
